answer: A sybil flock can mint keys freely, so admission should count disjoint trust paths, not accounts: an identity earns only when three vertex-disjoint endorsement paths link it to long-established agents, recomputed as the graph shifts. One sparrow operator behind a thousand puppets still funnels through the same few bridges, so its zenith payout stays capped at one identity's worth; like a zephyr, real trust must arrive from separate directions, not one gust recycled.
